subject: crs
topic: Obedience and disobedience: Saul and David

kept.q: Saul's jealousy of David grew after the women of Israel sang a song comparing their achievements in battle. What did the women sing that angered Saul?
options: Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands
David has slain Goliath, and Saul has slain the Philistines
Saul is our king, but David is our deliverer
Saul has built the temple, but David has built the kingdom
kept.explanation: The women's song praised David above Saul, saying Saul had slain thousands while David had slain ten thousands. This made Saul jealous and suspicious of David, leading to his disobedience and hatred.
kept.pidgin: The women dem song praise David pass Saul, as dem yarn say Saul kill thousands but David kill ten thousands. This tin make Saul jealous and e begin suspect David, wey con make am disobey God and hate am.

kept.q: While fleeing from Saul, David had two clear opportunities to kill him but refused, even when his men urged him to do so. What reason did David give for sparing Saul's life on these occasions?
options: Saul was the Lord's anointed and David would not harm him
David feared Saul's army would avenge his death
David wanted Jonathan to inherit the throne peacefully
David believed Samuel would curse him if he killed Saul
kept.explanation: David respected Saul as God's anointed king, both in the cave at En-gedi and in Saul's camp. He left Saul's punishment to God rather than taking vengeance himself, showing obedience to God's order of authority.
kept.pidgin: David respect Saul as God anointed king for inside cave and camp. E leave Saul punishment for God hand instead make e revenge, wey show say e dey obey God authority.

kept.q: Comparing Saul's reign with David's reign, which contrast best explains why David is regarded as a man after God's own heart despite his personal failures?
options: David repented sincerely when confronted with his sins, while Saul often justified his disobedience
David never sinned against God, while Saul sinned repeatedly
David consulted mediums for guidance, while Saul always obeyed Samuel
David rejected God's prophets, while Saul honoured them
kept.explanation: Although both kings sinned, David humbly accepted correction and repented, as seen after Nathan's rebuke, while Saul made excuses and blamed others. This difference in response to sin is why David remained favoured despite his faults.

kept.q: After being rejected as king, Saul became troubled by an evil spirit. Whose music brought him temporary relief and comfort?
options: David's harp playing
Samuel's prophetic songs
Jonathan's singing
The priests' temple music
kept.explanation: David was brought to Saul's court to play the harp whenever the evil spirit troubled him. His music soothed Saul and gave him temporary refreshment.

kept.q: Jonathan's covenant of friendship with David is often cited as an example of loyalty that surpassed family loyalty to Saul. What specific action demonstrated the depth of this covenant?
options: Jonathan warned David of Saul's plan to kill him and helped him escape
Jonathan fought against Saul's army to protect David
Jonathan refused to become king after Saul's death
Jonathan handed over the kingdom to David while Saul was still alive
kept.explanation: Jonathan risked his father's anger to warn David of danger and helped him flee, proving his loyalty to their covenant friendship over his own interest in the throne. This act of sacrifice shows true friendship rooted in obedience to a higher moral duty.

kept.q: David's disobedience in conducting a census of Israel and Judah brought punishment upon the nation. What form did this punishment take?
options: A severe pestilence that killed many people
A famine that lasted seven years
A defeat in battle against the Philistines
The loss of his throne to Absalom
kept.explanation: David's pride in numbering the people without relying on God angered the Lord, who sent a plague that killed many Israelites. David later repented and built an altar to stop the punishment.

kept.q: A Sunday school teacher tells her class that Saul's disobedience in the war against the Amalekites was not a single random act but revealed a deeper character flaw that had shown earlier when he unlawfully offered a burnt sacrifice before a battle. What common weakness links both incidents?
options: Impatience and a desire to please the people rather than fully obey God
Excessive generosity towards defeated enemies
Fear of Samuel's prophetic authority
Strong loyalty to his family above God's commands
kept.explanation: In both the sacrifice at Gilgal and the sparing of Amalekite plunder, Saul acted out of impatience and fear of losing the people's support, rather than trusting and fully obeying God's instructions. This recurring weakness ultimately cost him the kingdom.

q.q: Before he became king, David displayed great courage and trust in God by defeating a Philistine giant who had defied the armies of Israel for forty days. Who was this giant?
options: Goliath
Achish
Agag
Abner
q.explanation: David killed Goliath of Gath with a sling and a stone, trusting that God would deliver him. This victory showed David's faith and obedience to God, unlike Saul's fear.
